items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: Howard Rumsey and so on and forth

ctx.x: It does make sense. We have a kind of event here every year that I organize and sometimes it’s much like a jazz party where I call one person and I say, “Bring a band. Bring whoever you would like.” What I don’t say or have a hard time saying is: it would be a plus if it was a diverse quintet and I find that hard to say.

It’s hard ‘cause you can’t — you know it’s hard to tell the musicians, you know, to change whatever the make-up of the group is or whatever. But it’s yeah — and I understand it and it’s something important and I understand that it’s important but again it’s just one of those things that I don’t think there’s any right way or wrong way to approach it. I think it’s just a case by case basis for us as to whatever we’re doing, whatever we’re focused on and how we can best address things the right way and be…

many layers that you deal with when you’re at the college. You know there’s many different layers. Whereas at the Jazz Institute there’s none of those layers you know. You can pretty much do things exactly — people get paid exactly how you need to get — you know all those things. At the college it’s a whole different thing as you well know. So again you have to adapt, you have to adapt to the circumstances, which is what we’ve always tried to do but I can say that I feel pretty good that we’ve not made…
